title: Two-sided LCU from approximate clean columns
author: /root/batch2_composition
question:
Let \(K=\mathbb C^r\) with \(r\ge1\) and distinguished basis vector \(|0\rangle\), and let \(H=\mathbb C^d\) with \(d\ge1\). Fix the order \(K\otimes H\). For \(j=1,\ldots,r\) let \(U_j:H\to H\) be unitary and \(c_j\in\mathbb C\), not all zero. Put
\[
\alpha=\sum_j|c_j|>0,\qquad A=\sum_j c_jU_j,
\]
\[
\omega_j=\begin{cases}c_j/|c_j|,&c_j\ne0,\\1,&c_j=0,\end{cases}
\qquad l_j=\sqrt{|c_j|/\alpha},\qquad r_j=\omega_j\sqrt{|c_j|/\alpha}.
\]
Here the symbol \(r_j\) is a vector coordinate, while \(r\) is the selector dimension. Let
\[
S=\sum_j|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes U_j.
\]

Available unitaries \(Q_L,Q_R\) on \(K\) have clean columns \(\widetilde l=Q_L|0\rangle\) and \(\widetilde r=Q_R|0\rangle\) satisfying the exact-representative bounds
\[
\lVert\widetilde l-l\rVert\le\delta_L,\qquad
\lVert\widetilde r-r\rVert\le\delta_R,
\qquad\delta_L,\delta_R\ge0.
\]
An available unitary \(\widetilde S\) on \(K\otimes H\) satisfies \(\lVert\widetilde S-S\rVert\le\eta\), \(\eta\ge0\), in induced Euclidean operator norm; \(\widetilde S\) need not preserve the selector. The specified composite uses the actual adjoint \(Q_L^\dagger\) exactly:
\[
\widetilde W=(Q_L^\dagger\otimes I)\widetilde S(Q_R\otimes I),\qquad
Jv=|0\rangle\otimes v,\qquad
\widetilde B=J^\dagger\widetilde WJ.
\]
All work of this mathematical interface is in \(K\otimes H\).

Derive the clean-column sandwich formula for \(\widetilde B\). Prove the exact target formula
\[
(\langle l|\otimes I)S(|r\rangle\otimes I)=A/\alpha
\]
and derive the approximate block-encoding guarantee
\[
\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert\le\alpha\min\{2,\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta\}.
\]
Your proof must explain why no operator-norm approximation of \(Q_L\) or \(Q_R\) to a chosen full PREPARE unitary is required, and must justify unitarity and contraction facts used in the estimate. For ideal \(S\) in the middle, explicitly compute the implemented coefficients \(\overline{\widetilde l_j}\,\widetilde r_j\) and prove their \(\ell^1\) deviation from \(c_j/\alpha\) is at most \(\delta_L+\delta_R\). Explain whether this coefficient route and the direct sandwich-norm route are alternative proofs or jointly necessary assumptions.

Suppose instead that one only knows
\[
\lVert\widetilde l-e^{i\theta_L}l\rVert\le\delta_L,\qquad
\lVert\widetilde r-e^{i\theta_R}r\rVert\le\delta_R
\]
for real phases \(\theta_L,\theta_R\). Derive the corresponding phase-shifted target and an explicit bound on \(\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert\) that includes the phase mismatch. Give a concrete unitary example with perfect separate state fidelities but wrong exact block, and state a sufficient phase relation that restores the previous guarantee. The question concerns exact block representatives, even if an isolated prepared state is physically unchanged by its global phase.

Prove that changing the off-clean columns of \(Q_L\) or \(Q_R\) while retaining unitarity and their clean columns cannot change \(\widetilde B\) for fixed \(\widetilde S\); give an explicit pair of unitary completions at operator distance \(2\) with the same clean column. Discuss zero coefficients, \(r=1\), \(\delta_L=\delta_R=\eta=0\), and the excluded all-zero coefficient case. Explain why the mathematical availability of prepared state vectors alone does not supply an executable adjoint, coherent SELECT, clean-work implementation or finite-bit resource guarantee. A successful clean projection need not occur deterministically.
assumptions: Finite complex selector and system spaces of dimensions r≥1 and d≥1, with a fixed distinguished clean selector basis vector and tensor order K⊗H.
Every U_j is unitary; coefficients c_j are not all zero so α=Σ_j|c_j|>0.
Q_L,Q_R,S̃ are actual unitaries and the specified composite uses the actual Q_L†; clean-column errors and SELECT error are certified in Euclidean/induced operator norms.
The principal branch compares exact clean-column representatives. The later phase branch replaces those estimates by phase-referenced estimates with real θ_L,θ_R.
conventions: Complex inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument; a bra ⟨l| therefore has coefficients conj(l_j).
Matrix products act on column vectors from the rightmost factor first. No transpose replaces the complex adjoint.
The clean block projects the selector at both ends; a nonclean rejected sector may remain in the full output.
The coefficient ℓ¹ route and direct sandwich route may be used as alternative sufficient derivations; neither is an extra hypothesis on the inputs.
No approximate inverse is substituted for Q_L†. State-generation access alone is weaker than the available-unitary interface assumed in the main branch.

mathematical_target: Derive a two-sided complex-coefficient LCU contract whose approximation depends only on phase-aligned prepared clean columns and SELECT operator error, with explicit phase-mismatched and unitary-completion boundaries.
reference_answer:
The coefficient assumptions give \(\alpha>0\), and \(|\omega_j|=1\), including the chosen value for zero coefficients. Therefore
\[
\lVert l\rVert^2=\lVert r\rVert^2=\sum_j\frac{|c_j|}{\alpha}=1,
\qquad \overline{l_j}r_j=\frac{c_j}{\alpha}.
\]
For a zero coefficient both coordinates are zero; the choice of its phase does not affect them. The actual clean columns \(\widetilde l,\widetilde r\) also have norm one because their preparation operators are unitary.

For a vector \(v\in K\), define \(K_v:H\to K\otimes H\) by \(K_vu=v\otimes u\). Its operator norm is \(\lVert K_v\rVert=\lVert v\rVert\), since \(H\) is nonzero and \(\lVert v\otimes u\rVert=\lVert v\rVert\lVert u\rVert\). Its adjoint is \(K_v^\dagger=\langle v|\otimes I\), with the same norm. In particular these maps are isometries, or adjoint contractions, when \(v\) is unit.

The SELECT operator is unitary: its orthogonal selector blocks obey
\[
S^\dagger S=\sum_j|j\rangle\langle j|\otimes U_j^\dagger U_j=I,
\]
and the reverse product is likewise the identity. Tensoring each actual preparation with the identity preserves unitarity, and their adjoints and products are unitary. Hence the specified \(\widetilde W\) is unitary. Since \(J=K_{|0\rangle}\) is an isometry, \(\widetilde B=J^\dagger\widetilde WJ\) is a contraction. Also
\[
\lVert A/\alpha\rVert\le\sum_j\frac{|c_j|}{\alpha}\lVert U_j\rVert=1.
\]
These statements do not assert that the full output remains in the clean selector sector.

The clean input and output factors depend only on their specified columns:
\[
(Q_R\otimes I)J=K_{\widetilde r},\qquad
J^\dagger(Q_L^\dagger\otimes I)=K_{\widetilde l}^\dagger.
\]
Consequently
\[
\boxed{\widetilde B=K_{\widetilde l}^\dagger\widetilde S K_{\widetilde r}
=(\langle\widetilde l|\otimes I)\widetilde S(|\widetilde r\rangle\otimes I).}
\]
This formula holds even when \(\widetilde S\) mixes selector labels. With ideal \(S\), expanding the orthogonal selector blocks gives
\[
K_l^\dagger S K_r=\sum_j\overline{l_j}r_jU_j
=\frac1\alpha\sum_jc_jU_j=A/\alpha.
\]
The conjugation on the left column is essential.

One direct norm proof inserts the two ideal columns and ideal SELECT in three steps:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde B-A/\alpha
={}&K_{\widetilde l-l}^\dagger\widetilde S K_{\widetilde r}\\
&+K_l^\dagger(\widetilde S-S)K_{\widetilde r}\\
&+K_l^\dagger S K_{\widetilde r-r}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The norms of the three terms are at most \(\delta_L\), \(\eta\), and \(\delta_R\), respectively. Here the actual right column, ideal left column and both SELECT operators have norm one. Thus no extra product \(\delta_L\delta_R\) or dimension factor is needed:
\[
\lVert\widetilde B-A/\alpha\rVert\le\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta.
\]
Independently the two contraction estimates give \(\lVert\widetilde B-A/\alpha\rVert\le2\). Multiplying the better bound by positive \(\alpha\) proves
\[
\boxed{\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert
\le\alpha\min\{2,\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta\}.}
\]
At no point was either complete preparation operator compared to an ideal unitary completion. Only its clean column and actual unitarity were used.

For the explicitly requested coefficient route, hold ideal \(S\) in the middle and set \(B_S=K_{\widetilde l}^\dagger S K_{\widetilde r}\). Its exact coefficients are
\[
B_S=\sum_j\overline{\widetilde l_j}\,\widetilde r_jU_j.
\]
For each index, write
\[
\overline{\widetilde l_j}\widetilde r_j-\overline{l_j}r_j
=\overline{(\widetilde l_j-l_j)}\widetilde r_j
+\overline{l_j}(\widetilde r_j-r_j).
\]
Summing absolute values and applying Cauchy–Schwarz twice gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_j\left|\overline{\widetilde l_j}\widetilde r_j-\frac{c_j}{\alpha}\right|
&\le\lVert\widetilde l-l\rVert\lVert\widetilde r\rVert
+\lVert l\rVert\lVert\widetilde r-r\rVert\\
&\le\delta_L+\delta_R.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since each \(U_j\) has operator norm one, this bounds \(\lVert B_S-A/\alpha\rVert\). Moreover,
\[
\lVert\widetilde B-B_S\rVert
=\lVert K_{\widetilde l}^\dagger(\widetilde S-S)K_{\widetilde r}\rVert\le\eta.
\]
Triangle inequality recovers the same approximate-block estimate and its contraction cap. These are two alternative proofs of the error bound. The problem requests the coefficient calculation as well, but neither proof is an additional assumption that the other must consume.

In the phase-referenced branch, replace the two reference vectors by \(l'=e^{i\theta_L}l\) and \(r'=e^{i\theta_R}r\). They are still unit. Put \(\Delta=\theta_R-\theta_L\) and \(e=\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta\). The exact ideal sandwich is now
\[
K_{l'}^\dagger S K_{r'}=e^{i\Delta}A/\alpha.
\]
Repeating the three-term norm estimate under the replaced hypotheses gives
\[
\lVert\alpha\widetilde B-e^{i\Delta}A\rVert\le\alpha e.
\]
For the originally requested exact representative, one obtains
\[
\boxed{\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert
\le\min\left\{2\alpha,\ \alpha e+|1-e^{i\Delta}|\lVert A\rVert\right\}.}
\]
In particular this is at most
\[
\alpha\min\left\{2,\ e+2|\sin(\Delta/2)|\right\}.
\]
The universal cap still holds because the two block contractions are unchanged. The sufficient phase relation \(e^{i(\theta_R-\theta_L)}=1\) restores the previous bound; a common left/right phase cancels. This is not claimed necessary for every special target: \(A\) can vanish through cancellation even though \(\alpha>0\).

Separate fidelities alone do not control this relative phase. For example take selector dimension \(r=1\), any nonzero \(H\), \(c_1=1\), \(U_1=I\), \(Q_L=1\), \(Q_R=-1\), and \(\widetilde S=S=I\). Then \(l=r=1\), \(\widetilde l=1\), \(\widetilde r=-1\). Both separate squared fidelities equal \(1\), but \(\widetilde B=-I\) while \(A=I\), so
\[
\lVert A-\alpha\widetilde B\rVert=2.
\]
This realizes the phase branch with \(\theta_L=0\), \(\theta_R=\pi\) and zero phase-referenced errors. It does not satisfy zero exact-representative right-column error; that error is \(2\). The counterexample therefore does not contradict the main theorem.

For fixed \(\widetilde S\), the sandwich formula shows that unitary completions with the same two clean columns have exactly the same clean block, independently of every off-clean column. An explicit pair on \(\mathbb C^2\), with first coordinate clean, is
\[
Q=I_2,\qquad Q'=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1).
\]
They share the first column and \(\lVert Q-Q'\rVert=2\). Either can replace a preparation having that clean column without changing the sandwich. This particular pair has no nontrivial one-dimensional analogue, because a one-dimensional unitary is determined by its only column; the phase-fidelity counterexample nevertheless already works in that dimension.

Zero coefficients cause no division by zero in the phase definition because they use the stated separate branch, and their ideal coordinates vanish. Approximate columns can have weight on those coordinates, which is included in the same error bound. If \(\delta_L=\delta_R=\eta=0\) in the exact-representative branch, then \(\widetilde B=A/\alpha\) exactly. This still does not imply deterministic clean success. For example take two selector labels, \(c=(1,-1)\), \(U_1=U_2=I\), and exact columns \(l=(1,1)/\sqrt2\), \(r=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\). Then \(A=0\) and the ideal clean block is zero, although all components are unitary and \(\alpha=2\). The all-zero coefficient case is different: it has \(\alpha=0\), so the displayed normalization formulas are undefined and the active construction does not apply. The zero operator can be realized by other specified constructions, but dividing by this \(\alpha\) is not one.

The proof assumes actual coherent unitaries and the actual adjoint in the displayed composite. A source of prepared state samples alone does not provide an executable adjoint, a coherent SELECT implementation, an inverse of an unknown preparation procedure, or a certificate that unmentioned workspace is clean. All work here is explicitly in the given registers. No finite-bit precision supplier, gate synthesis or resource bound is derived. Clean projection defines an accepted branch; it is not a promise that the entire output is clean.

rubric.criterion: Checks \(\alpha>0\), unit norms of ideal and actual columns, the identity \(\overline{l_j}r_j=c_j/\alpha\), and SELECT/product unitarity plus the contraction facts used later.
Derives the clean-column sandwich and the exact target \(A/\alpha\), with conjugation, register order and the actual left adjoint correct. Explains why only clean columns enter.

Proves the additive \(\delta_L+\delta_R+\eta\) operator bound and independent cap \(2\), with no unneeded product or dimension factor, obtaining the scaled minimum. A valid direct or coefficient route suffices for this criterion.

Computes the ideal-SELECT coefficients \(\overline{\widetilde l_j}\widetilde r_j\), derives their \(\ell^1\) deviation by Cauchy–Schwarz, and identifies the coefficient and direct sandwich routes as alternative sufficient proofs, not additional input assumptions.

In the replaced phase branch, obtains \(e^{i(\theta_R-\theta_L)}A\), gives a correct explicit phase-mismatch error bound and sufficient cancellation condition, and verifies a unitary perfect-fidelity/wrong-block witness without incorrectly assigning zero exact-vector errors.

Proves invariance under changes to off-clean columns for fixed \(\widetilde S\), and verifies a pair of unitary completions at distance \(2\) with the same clean column. This diagnostic overlaps known completion examples and is not a separate new core.

Handles zero coefficients, \(r=1\), zero errors and the excluded \(\alpha=0\) case; distinguishes exact clean block from deterministic cleanup and available coherent unitaries/adjoints from mere state preparation access and finite-bit costs.

common_errors.error: Use \(l_jr_j\) in general or \(\widetilde l_j\widetilde r_j\) without conjugating the left column.
common_errors.why_wrong: The left factor is a bra supplied by the actual adjoint; complex conjugation determines both coefficients and phase difference.

common_errors.error: Assume the same PREPARE must appear on both sides for every LCU.
common_errors.why_wrong: Squared selector weights are the same-column architecture. The explicitly specified two-sided interface uses conjugate left amplitudes times right amplitudes to encode complex coefficients.

common_errors.error: Require full preparation-unitary operator closeness to an ideal completion.
common_errors.why_wrong: The projected sandwich depends only on the clean columns and actual unitarity. The unused columns may differ maximally.

common_errors.error: Add a mandatory \(\delta_L\delta_R\) term or a dimension factor.
common_errors.why_wrong: The three-term decomposition uses actual unit vectors on the untouched sides; its bounds are additive without those losses.

common_errors.error: Use the ideal coefficient formula for a general selector-mixing middle operator.
common_errors.why_wrong: The sum \(\sum_j\overline{\widetilde l_j}\widetilde r_jU_j\) applies to ideal block-diagonal SELECT. General \(\widetilde S\) is handled by an independent operator perturbation bound.

common_errors.error: Treat independent phase-optimized column errors or perfect fidelities as zero exact block error.
common_errors.why_wrong: Left and right global phases leave a relative scalar phase on the block; it cancels only under the stated sufficient relation or a special target.

common_errors.error: Infer nonzero target or positive success from nonzero coefficient normalization.
common_errors.why_wrong: Nonzero coefficients may cancel to \(A=0\), even with \(\alpha>0\). Unitarity only gives contraction, not deterministic clean success.

boundary_cases.conclusion: Their ideal columns vanish and phase is explicitly set to 1. Approximate leakage into them is covered by the same norm bound.
No unused completion columns, but independent left/right phase remains relevant to the exact scalar block.
Exact \(\widetilde B=A/\alpha\); still no deterministic-success guarantee.
